key_insight: QMage proposes a coherent quantum search for crystalline materials whose first-principles properties meet specified targets within an error tolerance.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support inverse design for formation energy, band gaps, elasticity, and conductivity without relying on extrapolation from known materials.
method: Search coherently over atomic compositions, unit cell structures, and atomic positions.
Block-encode each configuration’s Hamiltonian, isolate its target eigenstate, and evaluate properties.
Amplify configurations satisfying the targets using fixed-point search, then measure candidates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports logical-qubit and Toffoli-depth cost estimates spanning a classically routine benchmark and targets where established methods are unreliable, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: QMage is designed for mature fault-tolerant quantum computers, so practical deployment depends on hardware capabilities and resource requirements not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
